personas.verdict: PASS — rewrites two rules, not one; pushes back harder than the mechanism requires. Disagrees with mid-layer-competent on Phase 2 (6 vs 7): the same @import beat reads as an unclaimed mechanism gap to this persona rather than 'solid, not electric.'

personas.name: fast-operator

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No authored conversation, pause, or comparison cue anywhere in the body — no 'discuss with', 'tell the room', 'share with the person next to you'. Every sentence (rule-naming, story-ticket read, location choice, wiring, automation shapes) is about the artifact or the student's own move with the agent, never about cohort management.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named; mood-floor (8+/10 per beat, <7 REVISE, 7 = facilitator-premium flag) applies to teaching beats only.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer Meta block names the mood target verbatim ('the rule sits in MY file at MY location... I'm not building it today — and that's the move'). All three phases are teaching beats across all three personas — no setup/launch beat to exempt. Scoring against the primary (mid-layer-competent) persona: 8/7/8 across phases, 8 at close — no beat below 7. Opinionated-senior dips to 6 at Phase 2 specifically (below the 7 facilitator-premium floor for that persona), tied to the same @import friction the pedagogy §16 accept-note already covers — recorded as persona disagreement, not averaged away, per this run's brief. Fast-operator stays at or above 7 throughout because the risk that persona surfaces is silent acceptance, not low mood — the two are independent axes here.

No shame-framing in student-facing body. 'The generic rule is the tell... needs rewriting into your words, or rejecting' frames the generic rule as an expected artifact to sharpen, not a mistake the student made. The wiring Note frames an un-wired file as inert plumbing ('sits on disk unread'), not a student error. Holds across all three personas — none of the three reads the body as blaming them, including fast-operator, whose miss is invisible to the persona precisely because the body never signals fault.

teaching_moment_disagreement: Personas disagree on whether the reject-or-rewrite forcing function (extract-the-task-shaping-rule-1's stop-and-ask) reliably lands. Per the story-judge template, a teaching moment a persona can skip makes the artefact fragile — but this specific fragility is not a new finding: the file's own <!-- backing --> Stance block already names it as the open question ('contested: nothing evidential... would-move-it: rooms reporting that the surfaced rules come back generic anyway despite the rejection pass — a delivery signal, answerable from cohort notes'). This run's fast-operator persona is corroborating evidence for that standing question, reported here rather than filed as a fresh REVISE.
